title: Homepage & Product Copy Experiments — compact brief
content:
Purpose:
Short, scrappy brief capturing hero and product page copy variants we want to iterate on for the main marketing site. This is an early working doc — goal is to surface a few distinct positioning angles, prioritized headline + subhead pairings, and concrete A/B test plans. Keep things lean; we will port finalists into the /marketing PR for QA and design refinements.

TL;DR / hypothesis:
- Primary audience: product engineers and infra/platform teams evaluating hosted and private inference options.
- Core message should emphasize: predictable inference economics, production reliability, and a unified API across deployment modes.
- Hypothesis to test: engineering buyers respond more to concrete unit-economics + latency SLO language than to generic "best model" claims.

Hero tagline candidates (short list — prioritize 1,2,3 for A/B):
1) "Predictable inference. Any model. Any infra."
2) "Ship LLM features without the inference guesswork."
3) "High-performance inference, one API across hosted, dedicated, and private."
4) "Cut token cost, keep quality — inference tuned for production."
5) "Enterprise-grade LLM inference that scales with your product."
6) "Turn models into product features — fast, reliable, cost-aware."
7) "Ship faster. Pay less. Keep control."
8) "Latency SLOs, cost-aware serving, one dev experience."
9) "Run inference where you need it — cloud, reserved GPUs, or your VPC."
10) "Performance-first inference for real product teams."

Supporting subhead / one-liners (pick to match above):
- "Unified API, measurable unit costs, and automatic fallbacks to keep apps online."
- "From prototype to production: transparent benchmarks, rollout controls, and observability."
- "Reserved capacity, private deployments, or hosted API — same interface, predictable behavior."
- "Automatic batching, KV caching, and model routing that lower per-token spend."

Product page headline + subhead drafts (one or two variants each):
- Redwood API (hosted)
  Headline: "Hosted inference for rapid shipping"
  Subhead: "Start with a simple REST API, stream responses, and scale without ops — pay per-use."

- Redwood Dedicated
  Headline: "Reserved GPU capacity with SLA-backed performance"
  Subhead: "Predictable throughput and isolated capacity for mission-critical features."

- Redwood Private
  Headline: "Private control plane for regulated and sensitive workloads"
  Subhead: "Bring your own VPC, KMS, and ops integrations — air-gapped options available."

- Redwood Console (observability & rollouts)
  Headline: "Know cost, latency, and quality — in one place"
  Subhead: "Per-route dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and rollout controls to prevent regressions."

- Redwood Optimize
  Headline: "Optimize inference economics without sacrificing quality"
  Subhead: "Model and quantization recommendations, batching suggestions, and quality regression alerts."

Key value props (short bullets for homepage):
- Predictable unit economics: clear per-token and per-embedding cost with recommendations to lower spend.
- Production reliability: SLA tiers, automatic fallbacks, and canary/A-B rollouts.
- Developer-first UX: single API across hosted/dedicated/private, SDKs, and fast onboarding.
- Performance engineering: GPU-optimized runtime, KV caching, and batch-aware scheduling.
- Security & compliance: VPC, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logs, and enterprise support.

Competitive framing notes (quick brain-dump):
- Against big cloud AI services: emphasize predictable unit economics and uniform API across private/dedicated — rather than vendor lock. Call out transparent benchmarking vs opaque managed endpoints.
- Against LLM API providers (simplicity-first): highlight enterprise controls, SLAs, and private deployment options. Simplicity is fine for prototypes, but we solve for production fragility.
- Against self-hosted inference runtimes: stress the orchestration + ops + billing/analytics narrative — teams buy more than runtime kernels; they buy predictable operations and support.

Positioning playbook (3 angles to test):
A) Cost-first: "Reduce per-token spend by X% (case study)" + technical bullets on batching/quantization. CTA: "Estimate savings" (calculator).
B) Reliability-first: "Latency SLOs and fallbacks to keep product UX smooth" + fault-tolerant routing example. CTA: "See uptime guarantees" (SLA doc).
C) Developer-first: "One API from prototype to private production" + quickstart + SDK examples. CTA: "Get started — free credits".

Homepage layout sketch (content blocks):
- Hero + 2 CTAs (Get started / Estimate savings)
- Trust logos + quick metrics (latency 50–200ms, X% cost reduction sample)
- 3-column features (economics, reliability, control)
- Product cards (API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize) with one-line benefits and links to deeper pages
- Customer stories / short quotes (engineer-led outcomes)
- CTA band + footer links to docs, pricing, and enterprise contact

Experiment matrix & metrics:
- A/B hero tests: variants 1,2,3 (see above) — primary metric: signup conversion rate from hero CTA; secondary: docs click-through, pricing page visits.
- Mid-funnel test: Cost-first vs Reliability-first product page — metric: demo requests / enterprise contact.
- Qualitative: run 10 user interviews with engineering buyers to validate top messaging (run concurrently).
- Success thresholds: +15% relative lift in signup conversion or clear directional qualitative feedback.

Testing plan (6 weeks, high-level):
Week 0: finalize 3 hero variants, prepare assets + tracking (feature flags).
Week 1–3: run A/B across 50/50 split, capture early signals.
Week 4: analyze, run quick user interviews to explain behaviors.
Week 5–6: iterate with finalists, run second round (hero + product page combos).

Open questions / assumptions to validate:
- Do engineering buyers care more about explicit cost numbers on hero, or high-level messages about reliability?
- How credible are our claimed savings? Need at least 2 solid case examples or a calculator to back headline savings.
- What legal/compliance copy is needed for Private product page (customer must provide KMS, etc.)?

Notes-to-self / implementation details:
- Marco: can you share the latest benchmark numbers we can display (p50/p95 latencies by model class)? Link JIRA-4321.
- Emily: draft short customer quote from ACME that mentions cost and uptime — we need at least one engineering-focused quote.
- Jonah: coordinate with design to produce 3 hero art directions (tech-focus, business-focus, hybrid).

Next steps:
- Lock 3 hero + 3 product-page combos by EOD Friday.
- Create PR in /marketing with copy + hero art placeholders. See linked PR for process.
- Schedule 10 interviews (solutions engineering + growth to run).

Appendix (copy experiments log):
- 2024-10-21: initial draft - Aisha
- 2024-10-23: added cost-first variants - Marco
- 2024-11-08: updated metrics and test plan - Emily

Rough wireframe / copy snippets for dev landing (to port to docs):
- CTA button text ideas: "Start free", "Estimate cost savings", "Request dedicated capacity"
- Short FAQ bullets to include on product pages: "How does Dedicated differ from Hosted?", "Can I bring my own model?", "What happens during capacity exhaustion?"

End of brief.
